summary: We are designing two or three new Venturis for bench testing the week of November 30. Only the bore shape changes. The aim is a dose that stays steady on piped flow from 6 to over 100 L/min, still works at 6 L/min, and doesn't overflow the handpump.
Right now the lab PC is running the first round of 2-D simulations: 15 shapes at 7 flows from 6 to 120 L/min. Results expected this evening.
goal: Dose consistent from 6 to 100+ L/min. A max/min ratio of 2.67 or less keeps one needle setting inside 0.3–0.8 mg/L; we're aiming for about 2.2.
0.3–0.8 mg/L ideally, 0.1–2.0 acceptable, under 1.5 for taste. No overflow on the Afridev.
Bore shape only, no added parts. Body 125 mm max. Same 1" thread, injector port, fittings and needle valve.
plan: Round 2: refine around the best shapes
3-D check of the finalists on both reducers, 6–120 L/min
CAD files of the top two or three, ready to print by November 29

findings: On piped flow, how even the dose is depends on how port suction grows with flow. V1 (14 mm) overdoses at high flow; V3 (18 mm) underdoses at low flow. In the 1-D estimate a throat of about 16.5–17 mm comes out best, within about 2.2× from 6 to 100 L/min.
At 6 L/min nearly all the suction comes from the water column below the port, so the outlet must run full. A 26 mm outlet is marginal there; a slightly narrower outlet should fix it.

On the handpump, weak dosing at low pump rates happens because the Venturi stops running full. Air from the pump head reaches it when the level drops below the inlet bore. Shape can move this window but not widen it much, so some handpump variation will remain.
Bench V1 on the handpump already stays inside the acceptable 0.1–1.5 mg/L band from 7 to 26 L/min.

log: New goal: steady dosing from 6 to 100+ L/min on piped flow, changing only the bore shape. The vent idea was dropped. Round 1 of the 2-D screen started.
Narrower throats (10–12 mm) simulated in 3-D. They give more suction but overflow the handpump between 15 and 23 L/min. No fixed throat covers 10–20 L/min on the handpump.
Two-phase simulation of V1 on the handpump at 13 L/min. The pump head drains, air reaches the Venturi, and dose drops to about half.
